tone_statements.quote: Tonal systems are consistently absent in the Torricelli languages (relevant here are the One varieties), and the western languages (Sentani, Tobati, Ningera). The tonal systems in the phonologies of the Skou family languages are completely dominant, and remarkably comparable (Donohue 2003). Tonality in the Serra Hills languages varies inversely with their distance from the Skou languages, suggesting that tone is an areal phenomenon … Table 4: Comparative suprasegmental inventories … Pitches … Nasalisation … Border Ningera N

tone.says: Described as non-tonal: tonal systems are absent in Ningera, and its suprasegmental inventory shows no pitch contrasts, only contrastive nasalisation. Nothing said on word stress.
